subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation - FinEdge
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation - FinEdge

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. High level notes below.

Pain points you mentioned:
- Recent customer-impacting incident (Sept) where your in-house inference cluster lost capacity during a deployment, causing 2 hours of degraded latency and partial failures for critical billing flows.
- Limited ability to fail over across regions quickly; manual cutovers are slow and error-prone.
- Cost of keeping over-provisioned capacity to absorb spikes.

Current stack / constraints:
- On-prem + AWS EKS for model serving (custom runtime).
- Central SRE team manages deployment calendar tightly; limited ops bandwidth for building multi-region failover.
- Regulatory requirement to keep audit logs and encryption controls (KMS) for certain customers.

Success criteria you outlined:
- Reduce production incidents related to inference by 90% (compared to last 6 months).
- Meet p95 inference latency < 300ms for critical routes and maintain 99.95% availability for the inference path.
- Ability to failover to a secondary region (or a lighter-weight fallback model) within 3–5 minutes with automatic routing.

Reliability & graceful degradation items we discussed:
- Automated fallback models: run smaller quantized model variant when primary fails (preserves functionality with lower cost).
- Region failover: policy-based routing + health checks to move traffic to secondary region plus automated cache warming.
- Caching and batching to reduce critical path cost and smooth bursts.
- Observability hooks: token-level cost/latency breakdown, traces for root-cause.

Attachments: I attached a short SLA_summary.pdf and the Redwood product sheet with Dedicated/Private options.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with your SREs and our Solutions Engineer (Marissa) — 60 minutes. Proposed slots: Mon 12/1 10am PT or Tue 12/2 2pm PT.
2) Share incident post-mortem for the Sept outage (if possible) so we can map mitigation strategies.
3) We’ll prepare a short reliability playbook: fallback model options, suggested SLOs, and a cost rough-order estimate for a Dedicated pool vs. routing policy.

Would you prefer Mon 12/1 10am PT for the deep-dive?

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finedge.com>

Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation - FinEdge

Ben —

Appreciate the thorough recap. That matches our thinking. A couple of clarifying details from our side:
- The Sept incident was triggered by a canary rollout that accidentally scaled down the KV cache service; most failures were at peak 800 rps and lasted ~2 hours. We can share the incident post-mortem next week.
- For fallback models, we want to ensure degraded outputs are traceable and labeled in logs for downstream billing reconciliation.
- Our procurement timeline: aiming to finalize vendor selection by end of December; procurement will need initial SLA and pricing for committed capacity.

We can do Mon 12/1 10am PT for the technical deep-dive. Please include Marissa for the SRE-focused agenda. Also include any SOC 2 / compliance links you can share in advance for our security team.

Thanks — looking forward to the playbook.
Alex

--
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Reliability | FinEdge
alex.turner@finedge.com

Perfect — thanks Alex. Confirmed for Mon 12/1 10am PT. Agenda I’ll send today:
- 10m: Introductions & goals
- 15m: FinEdge incident walk-through (if you can share highlights)
- 25m: Redwood reliability architecture (fallback models, region failover, SLO suggestions) — Marissa will lead
- 10m: Next steps (trial/Dedicated sizing + procurement ask)

Attached: SLA_summary.pdf and product sheet. For SOC 2 and compliance materials, here are two links that should help your security team: https://docs.redwood.ai/compliance/SOC2-overview and https://docs.redwood.ai/compliance/data_handling. We’ll drop a short packet into the HubSpot record as well.

Marissa — can you take point on the deep-dive and come prepared to discuss:
- Fallback model options (quantized variants, expected quality delta)
- Region failover design and automated cache warming approach
- Typical observability outputs we can surface to FinEdge SREs during a trial

Alex / Priya — if there are any specific tests you want us to run during a trial (latency targets, throughput ramp, chaos scenarios), please share before Monday so we can prepare.

See you Monday.

Best,
Ben

Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Alex
